title: Mandatory reporting obligations that institutions routinely ignore
p1:
Many institutions have rules on paper that look strong. But the biggest risk often comes from what they fail to report.

A silence that seems harmless today can become a serious legal problem tomorrow.
p2: A common misconception is that reporting duties are only triggered after something becomes a major incident. In reality, many laws require institutions to report certain concerns at an early stage, even when facts are incomplete.
p3:
Schools, companies, hospitals, and other organisations may have mandatory reporting responsibilities for issues like abuse, financial wrongdoing, workplace misconduct, or regulatory violations. Ignoring these duties can create liability not just for the institution, but also for responsible individuals.

The practical lesson: having a policy is not enough. Institutions need clear systems that help people recognise, record, and report issues before they escalate.
conclusion: Do you think most institutions ignore reporting obligations because they are unaware of the rules, or because they fear the consequences of reporting?
